Compare with Regressions on Predicted Labels

Source: R/compare_hard.R
compare_hard.Rd

Replacing the class probabilities by a predicted label (the most likely class, or a confidence threshold) is a coarsening of the probabilities. compare_hard() reports, next to the soft_lm() estimate, two hard-label estimates on the same data, the distortion that coarsening causes, and the coverage that hard-label confidence intervals can be expected to have.

Usage

compare_hard(
  object,
  rule = c("argmax", "threshold"),
  threshold = 0.5,
  level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'softcats_hard'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

object

[mandatory] (softcats) A fit returned by soft_lm().

rule

[optional] (character) "argmax" assigns the most likely category; "threshold" (two categories only) assigns the non-reference category when its probability exceeds threshold (default: "argmax").

threshold

[optional] (numeric) Threshold for rule = "threshold" (default: 0.5).

level

[optional] (numeric) Confidence level for the intervals and the implied coverage (default: 0.95).

x

[mandatory] (softcats_hard) Result of compare_hard().

digits

[optional] (integer) Number of significant digits to print (default: 3).

...

[optional] Not used.

Value

An object of class softcats_hard: a list with estimates (a data frame with columns method, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high), the estimated distortion matrix distortion, the retention coefficients retention, and coverage, a data frame with the implied bias of the cross-fitted hard-label estimate and the implied coverage of its intervals. The print method returns x invisibly.

Details

The two hard-label estimates are:

  • hard (OLS): least squares of the outcome on the label dummies and the controls entered linearly, with HC1 or, with clusters, CR1 standard errors as in exclusion_test(). This is the analysis most often run in practice.

  • hard (cross-fitted): the same estimator as soft_lm() with the label \(h\) in place of the probabilities, using the same learner, folds and standard errors. Under the assumptions of soft_lm() it converges to \(A \tau\), where \(A = E[a_h a_h^\top]^{-1} E[a_h a^\top]\) is the coarsening (distortion) matrix, \(a_h\) the label after partialling out the controls and \(a\) the residualised probabilities. For two categories \(A\) is the attenuation factor \(\kappa\).

With more than two categories the distortion need not be uniform: the estimate for one category can also pick up the effects of the others, and the retention coefficients \(s_j = v_j^\top A v_j\) along the eigenvectors \(v_j\) of \(E[a a^\top]\) can differ across directions and need not lie in \([0, 1]\).

The implied coverage is an asymptotic approximation to the coverage of nominal Wald intervals for the cross-fitted hard-label estimate, \(\Phi(z - \nu) - \Phi(-z - \nu)\) with \(\nu\) the implied bias \((\hat A - I)\hat\tau\) divided by the hard-label standard error. It is an estimate: it uses the soft-label estimate in place of the true effects.

The regressions of the labels on the controls use the folds, the learner and the seed of the fit, so repeated calls on a fit with a seed give the same results.

References

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). Coarsening latent-class probabilities: Directional distortion and coverage loss. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.11784

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). When to trust static confidence thresholding: Calibration diagnostics for pseudo-labelled regression. Knowledge-Based Systems, forthcoming. Earlier version: doi:10.48550/arXiv.2605.12780

See also

kappa_curve() for the attenuation across thresholds.

Examples

# Example: Most likely category with three categories
d <- sim_softcats(n = 2000, K = 3, seed = 5)
fit <- soft_lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = ~ prob_A + prob_B + prob_C,
               data = d, learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 5)
compare_hard(fit)
#> Soft probabilities versus predicted labels (most likely category)
#> Difference from reference category 'A'
#> 
#>               method term estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>                 soft    B    1.120    0.1410    0.846     1.400
#>                 soft    C   -0.459    0.1370   -0.727    -0.190
#>  hard (cross-fitted)    B    0.660    0.0812    0.501     0.819
#>  hard (cross-fitted)    C   -0.411    0.0801   -0.568    -0.254
#>           hard (OLS)    B    0.652    0.0815    0.492     0.812
#>           hard (OLS)    C   -0.416    0.0802   -0.573    -0.258
#> 
#> Distortion matrix A (the cross-fitted hard estimate converges to A tau):
#>        B      C
#> B  0.546 -0.134
#> C -0.119  0.536
#> Retention along the eigen-directions of E[aa']:
#>  dir1  dir2 
#> 0.667 0.415 
#> 
#> Implied bias and coverage of nominal 95% hard-label intervals:
#>  term implied_bias std.error_hard coverage
#>     B       -0.448         0.0812 0.000188
#>     C       0.0796         0.0801    0.832
